# Nabd Plus Phase 0 findings register — v1

Baseline: `22526bedb77a3d8148219036367e4714f401aecc`
Scope: source audit only; no remediation.

## Verification gaps (not findings yet)

These require source/contract/runtime evidence before classification: all six-locale translation completeness; accessibility labels and keyboard behavior; cache-control and PHI exposure in every helper; exact Backend ownership responses; migration/database evidence; outbox/event delivery; live payment provider settlement/refund; sandbox replay; Docker/CI; and visual parity against every Mobile screen.

## Product decisions required

The owner must decide launch scope for read-only versus commerce; pharmacy prescription acceptance and split-order rules; cash/insurance/payment/refund/expiry; home-care provider versus queue model; chat/realtime scope; family consent; notification update scope; indexing/noindex policy; and whether agent-native payment protocols (x402/MPP/UCP/ACP) are in the launch contract.

## Rule

A finding is not closed by a passing build or by a UI placeholder. Closure requires code evidence, contract evidence, security/ownership tests, state/error tests, locale/accessibility review, and live or approved sandbox evidence where the behavior is transactional.

## Finance Engine findings added during Phase 0B

| ID | Severity | Finding | Direct evidence | Required acceptance condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-099 | P0 | Finance Engine’s money-moving idempotency is implemented as check-then-write/saga sequences rather than an atomic reservation or transaction: ledger `exists` precedes append, refund prior-check precedes gateway/wallet/ledger work, provider debit checks precede append, loyalty refund checks precede credit/insert, and approval execution precedes status update. Replay or concurrency can duplicate money movement or leave divergent gateway, wallet, ledger, booking and operation state. | `src/modules/finance-engine/finance-engine.module.ts:101–104,404–423,549–615,617–637,829–850`; `audit-artifacts/phase0b-backend/semantic-evidence-finance-engine-module.md` | Introduce and prove atomic unique keys/conditional transitions or transactions plus an outbox/compensation strategy; test concurrent replay, crash after each side effect, gateway retry and exact-once financial outcomes. |

| ID | Severity | Finding | Direct evidence | Required acceptance condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| F-146 | P1 | Care-program endpoint returns hard-coded Arabic programs, rewards, session text and a fixed `09:00` time; it only defines diabetes/pregnancy masters while accepting arbitrary program/session values, so product state and displayed schedule can be untruthful. | `src/modules/nabd-extensions/nabd-extensions.service.ts:283–371` | Source program catalog/schedule/rewards from governed data, validate enums/session membership, persist real completion state and test empty/unavailable states without fabricated values. |
| F-147 | P1 | Provider matching/ranking returns broad provider records and uses inconsistent location fields (`geo` versus ProviderProfile `location`); ranking substitutes constant rating/SLA/cancellation metrics and optional sponsorship, producing non-truthful ordering. | service `:377–433, 483–508`; `src/schemas/provider-profile.schema.ts:49–59, 128–132`; controller `:116–130` | Use canonical geospatial/indexed queries and real versioned metrics, validate coordinates/type, enforce public projection/PII redaction and ranking explainability tests. |
| F-148 | P0 | Nursing attendance/checklist and inventory flows lack service-layer ownership/provider/role checks; attendance uses a Riyadh default coordinate when booking location is absent, while checklist and inventory can be queried by identifier/account without scope. | service `:564–631`; controller `:142–161` | Reject missing location rather than fallback, authorize nurse/provider/patient relation and visit state, scope inventory to authenticated provider, validate coordinates and audit access. |
| F-149 | P1 | SLA cron and fraud detection are not concurrency-safe: SLA selects and updates orders without claim/lease or unique breach key; fraud uses check-then-create; broad catches silently suppress operational/collection errors. | service `:435–481, 510–558` | Add atomic claims/leases, unique event keys, observable error handling/retry/dead-letter policy and multi-worker duplicate/concurrency tests. |

| F-151 | P0 | Corporate credit lookup uses `companyName` only and ignores `employeeId`; it increments usedCredit and saves without atomic reservation, idempotency or employee/company authorization, permitting cross-employee misuse and race overspend. | service `:688–701`; controller `:190–193` | Resolve canonical corporate/employee identity, validate amount, atomically reserve within limits with idempotency/audit and concurrency/authorization tests. |

| ID | Severity | Finding | Direct evidence | Required acceptance condition |

| F-154 | P1 | Lifecycle event handlers create notifications without a durable event idempotency key/outbox or transition deduplication; repeated event delivery can duplicate patient/provider/admin notifications and deep links. | `src/modules/notifications/notifications.service.ts:316–852`; `src/schemas/notification.schema.ts:21–29` | Persist source event identity/version, unique dedup key and durable outbox/consumer retry semantics; test replay, ordering and partial failure. |
| F-155 | P1 | User/role/all listing exposes stored params/action/delivery metadata and role broadcasts through a broad `$or`; event params can carry PHI, insurance or finance amounts into push/SMS/WhatsApp/email without a visible sensitivity policy or projection/redaction boundary. | service `:280–295, 322–852`; schema `:9–24` | Define channel-specific least-privilege projections, audience isolation, PHI/financial redaction and retention/expiry; test patient/provider/admin cross-audience access. |

| F-157 | P1 | Notification payloads use raw title/body keys in email HTML and provider payloads, with no visible escaping/sanitization; arbitrary action routes/payloads are serialized into push deep links, creating content injection and route-confusion risk. | service `:159–165, 207–209, 246–254`; controller `:46–58` | Resolve trusted localized templates, escape HTML, allowlist deep-link routes/payload shapes, classify sensitive content and test malicious input. |
| F-158 | P1 | Notification controller defines `POST ':id/read'` before `POST 'read-all'`; depending on Nest route matching, literal `read-all` can be captured as an id route, and read operations have no idempotency/read-event audit beyond `read_by`. | `src/modules/notifications/notifications.controller.ts:36–44`; `src/modules/notifications/notifications.service.ts:298–314` | Make route matching unambiguous, add typed read contracts/idempotency and audit/read timestamp semantics, and test both paths and replay. |

## Redis findings added during Phase 0B

| ID | Severity | Finding | Direct evidence | Required acceptance condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-436 | P0 | Redis failure silently activates a per-process fallback for stateful primitives, so locks, idempotency, rate limits and security counters can diverge across replicas and may fail open during outage. | `src/modules/redis/redis.service.ts:15–23,105–159,308–313` | Classify primitives; fail closed for security/financial locks and test multi-replica outage behavior. |
| F-437 | P1 | Fallback implementations use non-atomic read/modify/write semantics for increment, setnx, sets and sorted sets, unlike Redis atomic commands, creating race-condition behavior under concurrent requests. | `src/modules/redis/redis.service.ts:139–159,218–277` | Use atomic scripts/transactions or disable fallback for correctness-critical operations; run concurrency tests. |
| F-438 | P1 | The shared `ready` flag is set true by any of three connections and false by any error, so client/subscriber/publisher health is not independently represented and event/state behavior can be misclassified. | `src/modules/redis/redis.service.ts:28–59` | Track connection roles independently and expose truthful health/readiness semantics. |
| F-439 | P1 | Pub/sub events are silently dropped when Redis is unavailable and subscribe returns without registration, with no durable replay/outbox or caller-visible degraded state. | `src/modules/redis/redis.service.ts:279–296` | Add durable event delivery/replay or explicit loss semantics and outage tests for notifications/workflows. |
| F-440 | P1 | `getClient()` exposes a partial raw client/shim whose fallback commands use storage semantics different from native hash/set/zset methods; callers can obtain `PONG` while Redis is actually unavailable. | `src/modules/redis/redis.service.ts:315–374` | Encapsulate command contracts, remove misleading health responses and test every advanced call-site against outage semantics. |
| F-441 | P1 | `checkRateLimit` performs `incr` then `expire` without atomic script/transaction and inherits fallback divergence, allowing window drift and race-based limit bypass. | `src/modules/redis/redis.service.ts:308–313` | Implement atomic fixed/sliding-window limit semantics with failover and concurrent tests. |
| F-442 | P1 | Connected `keys(pattern)` uses Redis `KEYS`, which can block Redis on large keyspaces and expose broad key-enumeration capability to callers. | `src/modules/redis/redis.service.ts:161–167` | Replace with bounded SCAN abstraction, restrict patterns and load-test keyspace behavior. |
| F-443 | P1 | `getJson` propagates malformed stored JSON without a typed corruption/degraded policy, while raw key/value APIs have no visible namespace, size, serialization or secret-value governance. | `src/modules/redis/redis.service.ts:298–305; src/modules/redis/redis.service.ts:105–167` | Add typed serialization/error handling, key namespace/TTL policies and secret/logging tests. |

| ID | Severity | Finding | Direct evidence | Required acceptance condition |

| F-686 | P0 | Per-IP/user/device counters are incremented sequentially with separate expiry operations and no visible atomic script, so concurrent requests can bypass limits or leave inconsistent windows. | `src/modules/api-security/api-security.module.ts:101–123` | Use atomic Redis operation with bounded failure handling and deterministic tests. |

| F-688 | P1 | Honeypot hits are intentionally returned as fake 200 success with empty data, making observability/client truthfulness ambiguous and potentially masking proxy/scanner mistakes. | `src/modules/api-security/api-security.module.ts:154–164` | Use explicit isolated sink/telemetry policy without contaminating product semantics. |
| F-689 | P1 | Route-class limits and enumeration detection rely on raw URL regexes/numeric path segments, vulnerable to route variants, encoded forms and false positives; fixed limits lack tenant/service context. | `src/modules/api-security/api-security.module.ts:24–32,86–145` | Use canonical route identity and versioned policy with adversarial/variant tests. |
| F-690 | P1 | Security events persist IP, device ID, user-agent, path and arbitrary extra fields without visible minimization, retention, access classification or redaction. | `src/modules/api-security/api-security.module.ts:54–70` | Define security-log schema, retention/encryption and least-privilege access. |
| F-691 | P0 | Global middleware executes for every route, including potentially health, webhook, auth and internal paths, without visible exclusions or trust-boundary policy; dependency/ordering effects may break critical integrations. | `src/modules/api-security/api-security.module.ts:217–226` | Explicit route matrix and integration tests for auth/webhook/health/CORS behavior. |
| F-692 | P0 | Rate-limit middleware short-circuits before Nest CORS and manually reflects a configurable/default origin list, creating policy drift and possible credentialed-origin exposure. | `src/modules/api-security/api-security.module.ts:166–184` | Centralize CORS policy and test disallowed/allowed credentialed responses. |
| F-693 | P1 | Blacklisting and rate-abuse logging are best-effort around Redis/event failures, with no durable reconciliation or operator-visible status when the security action cannot be persisted. | `src/modules/api-security/api-security.module.ts:80–84,111–119,154–168` | Durable abuse decision/event path or explicit degraded-security alerting. |
| F-694 | P0 | Blacklist clear accepts a raw key and deletes both IP and device namespaces, with no visible key-type validation, reason, audit event, approval or current-state result. | `src/modules/api-security/api-security.module.ts:209–213` | Privileged audited clear contract with explicit namespace and outcome. |
| F-695 | P1 | Admin security events returns raw event rows and grouped counts without time filters, pagination for counts, tenant scope or sensitive-field projection beyond Mongo `_id`. | `src/modules/api-security/api-security.module.ts:197–207` | Bounded redacted reporting with period/scope and auditable access. |
| F-696 | P1 | Global middleware trusts `req.ip` and connection fallback without visible proxy trust configuration, so deployment topology can alter rate-limit/blacklist identity. | `src/modules/api-security/api-security.module.ts:58–65,87–94,156–161` | Explicit proxy/IP canonicalization and deployment-specific tests. |

## MetricsInterceptor findings added during Phase 0B

| ID | Severity | Finding | Direct evidence | Required acceptance condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-1519 | P1 | Path normalization falls back to `req.url` and does not visibly remove query strings, so user-controlled query values can enter Redis hash fields and increase cardinality/PII risk. | `src/modules/ops/metrics.interceptor.ts:15–21,26–29` | Use route templates, strip query/fragment, bound and validate labels. |
| F-1520 | P1 | Normalizer only recognizes selected UUID/ObjectId/long numeric patterns; arbitrary identifiers, encoded values and malicious long paths can remain high-cardinality despite truncation. | `src/modules/ops/metrics.interceptor.ts:16–21` | Canonical route template mapping with bounded label registry. |
| F-1521 | P1 | Metrics omit HTTP method, tenant, actor, status reason and correlation ID, making admin analytics ambiguous and cross-tenant aggregation unsafe. | `src/modules/ops/metrics.interceptor.ts:24–31,37–52` | Explicit dimensions with PII-safe tenant/actor pseudonyms and access policy. |
| F-1522 | P1 | Sensitive endpoint paths are aggregated without a redaction/category policy, risking inference of patient, admin, payment or clinical operations from telemetry. | `src/modules/ops/metrics.interceptor.ts:28–41` | Sensitive-route categories and redacted labels. |
| F-1523 | P0 | Redis telemetry failures are silently swallowed, so loss of operational evidence is invisible and monitoring can falsely appear healthy. | `src/modules/ops/metrics.interceptor.ts:33–45` | Failure metric/alert, bounded retry and explicit telemetry health state. |
| F-1524 | P1 | Redis acquisition and `multi/exec` calls have no timeout, retry budget, backpressure or memory/cardinality control; a degraded Redis can amplify request latency/resource use. | `src/modules/ops/metrics.interceptor.ts:33–45` | Non-blocking bounded telemetry path with timeout and resource budgets. |
| F-1525 | P1 | Pipeline errors are ignored without checking per-command results, so partial increments/expiry failures can corrupt request and status totals. | `src/modules/ops/metrics.interceptor.ts:38–44` | Interpret pipeline results and reconcile or alert on partial failure. |
| F-1526 | P1 | Retention is set on daily keys only when a request records; abandoned/stale keys and key-count/cardinality growth have no cleanup or budget policy. | `src/modules/ops/metrics.interceptor.ts:29–44` | Explicit retention sweep, cardinality limits and memory monitoring. |
| F-1527 | P1 | Status classification defaults all successful interceptor completions to `res.statusCode || 200` and errors to `err.status/statusCode || 500`, without handling redirects, cancellations or custom error semantics. | `src/modules/ops/metrics.interceptor.ts:37–52` | Defined status taxonomy and edge-case tests. |
| F-1528 | P1 | Global telemetry executes after response completion/error through RxJS tap but has no guarantee for streams, aborted clients or headers-sent paths. | `src/modules/ops/metrics.interceptor.ts:48–52` | Request lifecycle instrumentation covering abort/stream/timeout cases. |
| F-1529 | P1 | Redis client access uses `(this.redis as any).getClient?.()`, bypassing compile-time API guarantees and allowing silent no-op when the client contract changes. | `src/modules/ops/metrics.interceptor.ts:33–36` | Typed metrics client contract and startup/health assertion. |
| F-1530 | P2 | Comment promises “every API call” and 14-day telemetry but the implementation bypasses non-HTTP traffic and has no evidence artifact/coverage assertion. | `src/modules/ops/metrics.interceptor.ts:5–10,24–25` | Accurate documentation and coverage/telemetry contract tests. |
